content: `ABogusPureSigner` is used as a process-wide singleton (`_pure_signer` in utils/dy_util.py) while this backend runs request handling in multiple threads (`ThreadPoolExecutor`, `threading.Thread`). `sign_query` mutates shared per-instance state: `self.counter += 1` is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent calls can read the same pre-increment value and emit duplicate counters, and interleaved `self._rand()` draws (global `random`) can mix sequences. Guard the counter (e.g. `itertools.count` or a `threading.Lock`) and/or use a per-call RNG so calls do not share mutable state.

content: `logger` is a process-wide loguru singleton, so this check-then-`setattr` sequence is a non-atomic read-modify-write. If two threads (e.g. a FastAPI worker thread and a daemon thread) call `install_code_logger_patch()` concurrently, both can observe an unpatched `orig` and each installs a wrapper around the other, producing a doubly-wrapped logger rather than the intended single wrap. Guard the install with a module-level `threading.Lock` (or `logger.remove`-style serialization) to make the idempotency claim actually hold under concurrency.
`import time` is never referenced anywhere in this module — dead import, remove it.

from loguru import logger

content: `rows` is always built with `lv: 0` (both here and in `recordsToRows`), so this condition `r.lv < 99` is always true and every row renders a `Lv.0` badge. When `lv` is a placeholder for unavailable data, the badge should be suppressed (e.g. `r.lv > 0 && r.lv < 99`) to avoid showing misleading level info.

`dmState` is keyed only by `uid`. When a comment has no valid uid, `String(c.uid || "")` yields `""`, so every such row shares `dmState[""]` and clicking 「私信」 on one row would visually update the state of all uid-less rows. Worse, because `sendOne` early-returns on empty uid the row stays disabled but the shared empty-string key remains a foot-gun. Key the state by the stable row identity instead (e.g. `c.cid || i`) or use a composite `${uid}:${cid}` key. Also note that the same `uid` appearing in multiple comments will share a single state entry, so a per-row key is more accurate.
suggestion_code:
const [dmState, setDmState] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
  // NOTE: dmState must be keyed per rendered row, not per uid (see below).
existing_code: const [dmState, setDmState] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});

content: `fmtNum` does not guard against non-finite values: `Infinity` passes every `>=` branch and produces `Infinity亿`, and `Number.NaN` is only caught because `Number.isNaN` is checked. Consider using `Number.isFinite(n)` instead of the null/undefined/NaN combination so `Infinity`/`-Infinity` also fall back to the placeholder.
suggestion_code: if (n === null || n === undefined || !Number.isFinite(n)) return "—";

content: `data` may not be a dict as assumed here. The endpoint's JSON could legitimately return a non-dict `data` (e.g. a list, or a JSON string) or `j` might be a list; in that case `len(data)` still succeeds but `data.get('err')` / `data.items()` lower down would raise `AttributeError`/`TypeError` outside any try block, crashing the probe. Since this is a diagnostic script whose whole purpose is to report failures, a malformed/error response is a plausible input. Guard the type (or wrap the consumption in try/except) before assuming a mapping.
existing_code:
data = j.get("data") or {}
        return el, len(data), data

content: The `HTTPError` handler parses the error body with `json.loads(...)` unconditionally. If the backend returns a non-JSON error body (empty body, plain-text, or an HTML 500 page), `json.loads` raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, which is not caught here and aborts the whole verification run mid-way — exactly when you most need the check output. Guard the parse and fall back to a raw-text/placeholder dict.
existing_code:
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode("utf-8") or "{}")

content: `stop_recv_daemon`/`stop_browser_daemon` validate the process by matching a label string only, while the actual kill is by OS pid; conversely the port is taken from the caller verbatim. There is no validation that the pid still belongs to the process originally registered (pid reuse after the daemon exits could cause `kill_tree()` to terminate an unrelated process tree). Prefer verifying the child is still the live one registered (e.g. check `is_alive()`/the stored `CommandChild` before issuing `taskkill /F /T`), and reject/verify `port` ranges before using them in labels or process arguments.
existing_code: let label = format!("recv_daemon({}:{port})", accounts.join(","));

content: The log-write command takes arbitrary frontend-controlled `text` and writes it unbounded into `logs/frontend_boot.log` with no size cap or rotation. A misbehaving or compromised webview can spam this call and grow the log without limit (and the file is never truncated). Bound the write (size/rate limit) and/or rely on the already-configured logger instead of a bespoke file path derived from the executable directory.
existing_code: writeln!(f, "{}", text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

content: The source-mode backend relies on the `py` launcher being on PATH; when `-DevBackend` is used on a machine without the launcher (or with only a Store placeholder) the process exits immediately and the user only sees the generic "[FAIL] 后端启动超时". Consider validating the interpreter/`py` availability up front and emitting a clear error (the sibling `build_sidecar.ps1` already codifies the "Store placeholder" pitfall).
existing_code:
Start-Process -WindowStyle Minimized -FilePath "py" `
        -ArgumentList "-X","utf8","backend/main.py" `
        -WorkingDirectory $ROOT
